caption: A chilled cocktail glass is set on a bar in a warm room, and a film of mist forms on it and turns into running drops.

sa.check: A chilled cocktail glass is set on a bar.
A film of mist forms on the glass.
The bar mat wets beneath the glass.
The setting down comes first and the misting follows.

pc.expect: The misting and beading only build while the glass stays cold: the drops grow, join and run.
pc.fail: The glass dries while it is still cold and frosted; or the glass mists and dries in turn; or the glass is misted before it is taken out of the chiller; or the beads shrink while the glass is still cold.

pc.expect: The drops run downward over the glass to its stem and foot and wet the bar mat.
pc.fail: A drop runs up the glass; or water gathers on the rim and stays as a dome; or a drop leaves the glass and rises; or a run travels sideways round the bowl and stays level.

pc.expect: The mist lies on the outside of the cold glass and the mat wets where runs reach it.
pc.fail: The mist forms on the inside of the glass; or the bar mat stays dry under a glass streaming with runs; or the mist forms on the bar beside the glass while the glass stays clear; or the glass mists before it is chilled.

pc.expect: The mist is a fine even film that beads into rounded drops which merge and streak, and the glass stays rigid.
pc.fail: Touching drops overlap without merging; or drops jump about on the glass; or the film peels away as a sheet; or the beads turn to hard frost while the glass runs with water.

pc.expect: One glass on one bar; the glass keeps its bowl and stem and nothing passes through it.
pc.fail: The glass changes shape; or a second glass appears; or the stem detaches; or the drink passes through the glass's wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The glass's shape, the drink's colour and the bar stay the same.
pc.fail: The glass changes pattern; or the drink changes colour; or items on the bar rearrange.
